key_insight: Latent Memory Palace (LMP) turns control “reasoning” into iterative retrieval in an autoregressive latent space, using variational inference to adapt how much computation a policy spends before acting.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to more flexible robot and control policies that can trade latency for decision quality and also produce better action tokenizers for downstream autoregressive control.
method: Models reasoning as an autoregressive latent-variable policy with a variational lower bound.
Optimizes the bound with a latent-space reinforcement learning objective.
Uses the same framework to build LMP-π for control and LMP-tok for variable-length action tokenization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong empirical performance in both simulation and real-world domains, with interpretable adaptive test-time compute and improved downstream autoregressive policy performance.
watch_item: Variational latent reasoning and autoregressive retrieval may add training complexity and inference overhead, so stability and runtime need careful validation on new control tasks.
paper_title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
